content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.
When this app is finished, what should be easier or different for you compared with how you handle bookmarks today?

Right now I keep bookmarks in my browser and it's a mess — I save a link and then can never find it again. So a few things would make my life easier:

- I want to just paste a web address and have it saved, and ideally the app grabs the page's title and a bit of description automatically so I don't have to type it all in.
- I want to organize them with tags, and be able to click a tag to see just those.
- I really want good search — searching by words in the title or description, and by tag — so I can actually find things later.
- A "read later" pile would help, so I can mark stuff to come back to and see just those.
- I'd like to edit or delete a saved link, and clicking one should take me to the actual page.

Longer term I'd also love things like saving a note on a link, keeping a saved copy of the page in case it disappears, and tidying up old ones by archiving instead of deleting. But the core of it is: save a link fast, tag it, and find it again later.

content:
What I understand is: the core goal is to quickly save a link, organize it with tags, and reliably find it later through search, tag filtering, or a read-later view. Editing, deleting, and opening saved links are part of that core. Notes, offline copies, and archiving can wait for a later cycle.

Is that the right direction?

Yes, that's the right direction. Saving a link fast, tagging it, and being able to find it again — by search, by tag, or in a read-later view — is exactly the heart of it, and editing, deleting, and opening links belong right there with it. I'm happy to leave notes, offline copies, and archiving for later.

One thing I'd want as part of that core save flow: when I paste a link, the app should pull in the page's title and description automatically so I'm not typing everything by hand. And if I happen to paste a link I've already saved, I'd rather it take me to edit the existing one than end up with duplicates. Other than that, you've got it.

content: If you paste an address that leads to an already-saved page but differs only by a section marker, a trailing slash, or advertising-tracking information, should the app still treat it as the existing bookmark and open it for editing?

Honestly, to me a link that's the same page but with a trailing slash or some tracking junk on the end is the "same" bookmark, so ideally the app would recognize it and take me to edit the existing one rather than make a near-duplicate — that's the same spirit as catching an exact repeat.

That said, I don't want to over-engineer this. A section marker that jumps to a different part of a page I could see being treated as its own thing, and I won't insist you nail every variation of a messy address. The important part — pasting the same link again lands me on the existing bookmark — is already covered. So trimming the spaces and matching regardless of capitalization so it reuses the existing "reference" is what I'd want.
